title: Verify local suite limits without wall-clock waits

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-277#observe-local-suite-waits

**Outcome: Caught.**

## Selected promise

- **Story:** SEED-277#observe-local-suite-waits (`.planning/seeds/SEED-277-observe-local-suite-waits.md#observe-local-suite-waits`), plan `.planning/slice-plans/537-observe-local-suite-waits/PLAN.md`.
- **Revision:** `84a3853a4f9ef1b6dced9fc0cbb7bebddadb8b85` (branch `claude/verify-local-suite-limits-without-wall-clock-wai`).
- **Promise (key example 2):** While a full suite holds admission, a contender in a linked worktree that carries a copied current token reaches the admission gate and the live owner blocks it. No contender checks start. A copied token without live ancestry does not count as inheritance.
- **Expected observable behavior:** the contender writes the `OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_ADMISSION_GATE` marker with the owner's record id, and starts no `start-*` checks before cancellation.

## Fault

- **Location:** `scripts/local-test-suite.mjs`, `acquireLocalSuite`, the inheritance check.
- **Change:** removed the live-ancestry condition, so a matching inherited token from a live owner is enough to skip admission:

```diff
-      living(previous) &&
-      lineage.has(previous.pid)
+      living(previous)
```

- **Why plausible:** this is the policy that separates a nested child from a contender that copied the token. The execution already fixed the copied-token key, which on macOS never reached this check. Dropping or bypassing the ancestry part would let any process with a leaked `DOUGH_LOCAL_SUITE_OWNERS` value run alongside the owner.

## Fixture and maintained assertion

- **Test:** `tests/support/local-test-suite.test.mjs`, "repository full suites serialize across spaced worktrees while focused and CI runs remain independent". This uses the controlled-suites fixture (`tests/support/local-test-suite-fixtures.mjs`), a real owner in the primary checkout, and contenders in a temporary linked worktree.
- **Assertion:** `assert.equal(await pretender.gate, original, ...)` in the `["stale-token", ownerRecord.tokens[0]]` loop. The `gate` promise comes from `repositoryAtAdmissionGate` in `tests/support/local-test-suite-gates.mjs`. It rejects when more than `limit: 0` checks mark their start before the marker appears. Neither the fixture nor the assertion was edited.

## Run observations

All runs used a separate detached scratch worktree at the selected revision (`/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/a9d0936a/tmp/ic-scratch`). I ran `npm ci` and `node scripts/setup-native.mjs browser` first, both exit 0. Every run used Node 24.21.0 (matching `.node-version`) and Homebrew Bash first on `PATH`, under `caffeinate -s -i`. The focused command was `npm test -- tests/support/local-test-suite.test.mjs`, with `OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_OUTCOMES` pointed at a scratch file to record the per-file outcome. The pre-probe `git status --porcelain` was empty.

1. **Baseline:** exit 0 (two runs). The outcomes file reported `passed tests/support/local-test-suite.test.mjs`. The runner's failures-only reporter does not list passing tests, so I also ran `node --test --test-reporter=spec` on the same file with `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` unset. It listed all 6 tests passing, including the selected test, with 6 pass, 0 fail and none skipped.
2. **Fault:** exit 1. The outcomes file reported `failed tests/support/local-test-suite.test.mjs`. The runner output had exactly one failing test, the selected one (`local-test-suite.test.mjs:58`):
   `not ok: repository full suites serialize across spaced worktrees while focused and CI runs remain independent` / `Error: 1 checks started before the admission gate`, thrown from `FSWatcher.inspect` (`local-test-suite-gates.mjs:29`).
   - **Reach and changed behavior:** the rejection comes from the `pretender.gate` observation, which is the intended assertion. It shows that the contender started a check (`start-*` marker) instead of being blocked. Only the copied-token iteration can trigger it under this fault. The `"stale-token"` value cannot equal the owner's UUID `tokens[0]`, so that contender still takes the unchanged blocking path. The nested-invocation test, which needs genuine ancestry inheritance, still passed. That shows the fault removed only the ancestry requirement and did not break inheritance in general. The stack trace does not name the loop iteration, so the copied-token attribution comes from this reasoning and was not observed directly.
3. **Restoration:** an EXIT/INT/TERM trap ran `git checkout -- scripts/local-test-suite.mjs`. Afterward, `git status --porcelain` matched the empty pre-probe snapshot and `HEAD` was still `84a3853a4`. The same focused command then exited 0, with the outcomes file reporting `passed`. I then removed the scratch worktree with `git worktree remove` and pruned it. The execution checkout was not touched, and its status stayed clean.

No pre-existing failures or flaky results appeared in any run.

## Costs

- **Test runtime.** Focused runner wall time, measured with Unix epoch ms around `npm test`: baseline 17616 ms and 17651 ms, fault 18497 ms, restored 20312 ms. The supplementary spec-reporter run reported `duration_ms 19132` (Node's test runner). Setup (`npm ci`, browser setup) was not timed separately.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human took part, and no separate measure of human time exists.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable. No separately supported measure, such as tokens or tool-call time, was exposed to this agent. The elapsed entry below covers wall time only.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 209546 ms (measured), from 1794153394567 to 1794153604113 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
